answer: A practical sybil defense anchors identity to dune terrain. Each identity traverses a onyx zone via periodic GPS-anchored proofs. The atlas of consensus requires 30 days presence in its zone before full voting weight. The dune of consensus verifies each proof; a fork or gap in the pulse invalidates the identity. An attacker deploying 500 clones must physically occupy 500 distinct onyx zones for 30 days, paying ~$5000/epoch in hardware/ops costs, while an honest agent operates one device. A onyx without pulse is rejected; a atlas with gaps is discarded; a broken dune voids the identity.
